qualifications_or_emphasis: Position of Managing Director vacant since 30.09.2023 with no successor appointed due to ongoing inter-se disputes amongst Promoters pending before Hon'ble NCLT
Company filed C.A. No. 47 of 2023 before Hon'ble NCLT seeking appointment of administrator without supersession of board
Hon'ble NCLT interim orders dated 27.09.2023 and 04.10.2023 mandated temporary arrangement where all major decisions to be collectively made by Board of Directors

Regulation 26A(1)- As Informed by the management, due to the ongoing inter-se disputes amongst the Promoter/ Promoters Group which are pending adjudication before the Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad in the matter titled as 'Mahendra Mohan Gupta &Ors. v. Devendra Mohan Gupta & Ors., C.P. No. 64 of 2023', the vacancy in the office of MD has remained beyond the 3- month period stipulated in Regulation 26A. However, we have been informed by the Company that it is currently operating in terms of the orders dated 27.09.2023 and 04.10.2023 passed by Hon'ble NCLT wherein it was directed that in the absence of a Managing Director and a special arrangement, any major decision would be taken
Compliance certificate issued solely for regulatory purpose, not assurance of future viability or management efficiency

Emphasis of Matter: Petition under Sections 241, 242 and 244 of Companies Act, 2013 filed by certain promoters against other promoters pending with NCLT; appeal filed with NCLAT against request from holding company to convene EGM for removal of directors; NCLAT directed implementation of EGM resolution kept in abeyance until NCLT petition outcome; management does not expect impact on financial statements

No proceedings have been initiated on or are pending against the Company for holding benami property under the Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (as amended in 2016) and Rules made thereunder.

The physical verification of inventory has been conducted at reasonable intervals by the Management during the year and, in our opinion, the coverage and procedure of such verification by Management is appropriate. The discrepancies noticed on physical verification of inventory as compared to book records were not 10% or more in aggregate for each class of inventory.

The Company has been sanctioned working capital limits in excess of Rs 5 crores, in aggregate, from banks on the basis of security of current assets. The Company has filed quarterly returns/statements with such banks, which are in agreement with the books of account.
In respect of the loans, the terms and conditions under which such loans were granted are not prejudicial to the Company's interest.

In respect of the loans, the schedule of repayment of principal and payment of interest has been stipulated, and the parties are repaying the principal amounts, as stipulated, and are also regular in payment of interest as applicable.
In respect of the loans, there is no amount which is overdue for more than ninety days.

There were no loans which have fallen due during the year and were renewed/extended. Further, no fresh loans were granted to same parties to settle the existing overdue loans/advances in nature of loan.
There were no loans which were granted during the year, including to promoters/related parties that were repayable on demand or without specifying any terms or period of repayment.
In our opinion, the Company has complied with the provisions of Sections 185 and 186 of the Companies Act, 2013 in respect of the loans and investments made, and security provided by it.
The Company has not accepted any deposits or amounts which are deemed to be deposits referred in Sections 73, 74, 75 and 76 of the Act and the Rules framed there under.
The Central Government of India has not specified the maintenance of cost records under sub-section (1) of Section 148 of the Act for any of the products of the Company.

In our opinion, the Company is generally regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues in respect of Income tax, though there has been a slight delay in a few cases, and is regular in depositing undisputed statutory dues, including provident fund, employees state insurance, duty of customs, cess, goods and services tax, Professional tax and labour fund as applicable, with the appropriate authorities. However, there are no arrears of statutory dues outstanding as at March 31, 2026, for a period of more than six months from the date they became payable.
There are no statutory dues referred to in sub-clause (a) which have not been deposited on account of any dispute.
There are no transactions previously unrecorded in the books of account that have been surrendered or disclosed as income during the year in the tax assessments under the Income-tax Act, 1961.
As the Company did not have any loans or other borrowings from any lender during the year, the reporting under clause 3(ix)(a) of the Order is not applicable to the Company.
On the basis of our audit procedures, we report that the Company has not been declared Wilful Defaulter by any bank or financial institution or government or any government authority.
The Company has not obtained any term loans.

According to the information and explanations given to us, and the procedures performed by us, and on an overall examination of the Standalone financial statements of the Company, we report that no funds raised on short-term basis have been utilised for long-term purposes by the Company.

On an overall examination of the Standalone financial statements of the Company, we report that the Company has not taken any funds from any entity or person on account of or to meet the obligations of its subsidiaries or associates.

According to the information and explanations given to us and procedures performed by us, we report that the Company has not raised loans during the year on the pledge of securities held in its subsidiaries or associate companies.
The Company has not raised any money by way of initial public offer or further public offer (including debt instruments) during the year.
The Company has not made any preferential allotment or private placement of shares or fully or partially or optionally convertible debentures during the year.

During the course of our examination of the books and records of the Company, carried out in accordance with the generally accepted auditing practices in India, we have neither come across any instance of material fraud by the Company or on the Company, noticed or reported during the year, nor have we been informed of any such case by the Management.

During the course of our examination of the books and records of the Company carried out in accordance with the generally accepted auditing practices in India, a report under Section 143(12) of the Act, in Form ADT-4, as prescribed under rule 13 of Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014 was not required to be filed by us, as statutory auditors, with the Central Government. Further, no such report has been filed by any other auditor appointed by the Company under the Act.
As the Company is not a Nidhi Company and the Nidhi Rules, 2014 are not applicable to it, the reporting under clause 3(xii) of the Order is not applicable to the Company.

The Company has entered into transactions with related parties in compliance with the provisions of Sections 177 and 188 of the Act. The details of related party transactions have been disclosed in the Standalone financial statements as required under Indian Accounting Standard 24 "Related Party Disclosures" specified under Section 133 of the Act.

In our opinion, the Company has an internal audit system commensurate with the size and nature of its business. The reports of the Internal Auditor for the period under audit have been considered by us.
In our opinion, the Company has not entered into any non-cash transactions with its directors or persons connected with the directors.

The Company is not required to be registered under Section 45-IA of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The Company has not conducted non-banking financial / housing finance activities during the year. The Company is not a Core Investment Company as defined in the regulations made by the Reserve Bank of India. In our opinion, the Group [as defined in the Reserve Bank of India (Core Investment Companies) Directions, 2025] does not have any CICs, which are part of the Group.
The Company has not incurred any cash losses in the financial year or in the immediately preceding financial year.
There has been no resignation of the statutory auditors during the year.

On the basis of the financial ratios, ageing and expected dates of realisation of financial assets and payment of financial liabilities, other information accompanying the Standalone financial statements, our knowledge of the Board of Directors and management plans and based on our examination of the evidence supporting the assumptions, nothing has come to our attention, which causes us to believe that any material uncertainty exists as on the date of the audit report that the Company is not capable of meeting its liabilities existing at the date of balance sheet as and when they fall due within a period of one year from the balance sheet date.

The Company does not have any amount remaining unspent under sub-section (5) of Section 135 of the Act as at balance sheet date in respect of "other than ongoing projects" of Corporate Social Responsibility.

The Company has transferred the amount of Corporate Social Responsibility remaining unspent under sub-section (5) of Section 135 of the Act pursuant to ongoing projects to a special account in compliance with the provision of sub-section (6) of Section 135 of the Act.

Emphasis of Matter: Petition under Sections 241, 242 and 244 of the Companies Act, 2013 filed by certain promoters and promoter group members against other promoters and promoter group members, pending with NCLT. Company filed appeal with NCLAT against request from holding company Jagran Media Investment Network Private Limited to convene EGM for removal of 7 independent directors and 1 whole-time director. outlook.statement: As we look ahead, we remain dedicated to fortifying these bonds, generating enduring value through authentic journalism and future-ready capabilities.

Print's relevance will increasingly be defined by its ability to leverage inherent strengths of trust, depth and meaningful engagement; focus on strengthening circulation quality, deepening reader connect and unlocking new monetisation levers through integrated, insight-led offerings.

Digital business accelerated investments into digital platforms, content capabilities and audience engagement initiatives to strengthen digital ecosystem, amplify audience engagement, expand presence across next-generation media formats and unlock future growth opportunities.

Outdoor and activation businesses well-positioned to generate significant long-term value given tilt towards engagement-led marketing strategies; strategic shift towards asset-led outdoor operations and growing demand for experiential brand engagement solutions.

Radio business underwent strategic recalibration to optimise operational efficiency and structurally position segment for sustainable growth; returned to positive operating profitability in Q4 FY26, laying resilient foundation for future value creation.

Focused on strengthening audience relationships, accelerating digital journey and expanding value across platforms for Radio City; backed by data, AI, distinctive IPs and extensive understanding of local markets.

Media leadership requires seamless integration of storytelling, technology and commerce; developing scalable platforms prioritising user trust and regional diversity; continuous investments in data, AI-driven personalisation and multi-format content (video, audio, immersive); building diversified, sustainable monetisation models.

OOH growth driven by digital formats (DOOH), transit media, premium assets (airport, luxury retail, iconic billboards), programmatic trading, hyperlocal expansion in Tier-2/3 towns, experiential marketing, event spend, and activation growth in Tier-2/3 towns; wedding/personal events and government events as revenue drivers.

As brands place greater emphasis on impact, accountability and relevance, OOH continues to evolve beyond traditional visibility. With focus on premium inventory, digital innovation, technology-led applications and integrated solutions, we are therefore charting a trajectory that is value-enhancing and sustainable.

Experiential marketing is evolving from isolated events to integrated brand ecosystems. As consumers seek more engaging participation, demand is shifting towards experiences that are scalable, technology-led and capable of creating lasting brand impact. Our focus remains on strengthening client partnerships, augmenting creative capabilities and delivering experiences that generate thriving outcomes.
Solar installations expanded to four new sites during the year, with additional locations planned for deployment in coming years as part of renewable energy roadmap
Continued focus on energy efficiency, emissions reduction, and water conservation through process improvements
The Company is actively encouraging the adoption of electric vehicles as part of its broader efforts to reduce fuel consumption and minimize its carbon footprint.
The Company recognizes the importance of systematic record-keeping and is committed to strengthening its documentation processes going forward.

The Company is evaluating the integration of assessments carried out by statutory authorities or independent third parties at its plants, with the aim of further enhancing its overall health and safety framework.

With the escalation of Gulf war, the prices of the newsprint have increased significantly, while the rupee has also weakened, but we expect the impact of these developments to be temporary and not permanent in nature.

Print industry expected to maintain stable performance supported by loyal readership; print-led events emerging as important revenue stream; focus on strengthening home delivery, engaging younger audiences, diversifying revenue, enhancing data analytics.
Radio business expected to report satisfactory growth in revenues and profits from next year onwards after cost rationalisation and restructuring.

Digital business focusing on direct traffic, captive audiences, cost rationalisation; monetisation strategy includes ad inventory, syndication, production house, branded content, events, content-to-commerce, subscriptions.
OOH media sector expected to witness stable growth, revenues projected ~INR 85 billion by CY2028 (CAGR >8%).
Organised live events segment expected to expand from INR 145 billion in 2025 to INR 196 billion by 2028.
Digital media sector projected to grow at CAGR 14% over next three years, reaching INR 1.3 trillion in 2026 and exceeding INR 1.6 trillion by 2028.
M&E industry projected to grow 2.8% to ~INR 2.9 trillion in 2026, then CAGR 6% to INR 3.3 trillion by 2028.

India's economic growth expected to remain around 7% in foreseeable future; currency expected to strengthen once global uncertainties ease, regain 4th largest economy position soon, potentially 3rd over next few years.

The Company operates in India and is not materially exposed to foreign exchange risk arising from foreign currency transactions. The Company generally deals in USD for newsprint purchases from outside India. Foreign exchange risk arises from future commercial transactions and recognised assets and liabilities denominated in a currency that is not the Company's functional currency (INR). The risk is monitored and measured in a volatile currency environment through dependable forecasts by the external resources and is addressed by exiting from the exposure in material cases.

The Company's main interest rate risk arises from borrowings with variable rates, which exposes the Company to cash flow interest rate risk. During March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, the Company's borrowings at variable rate were denominated in INR.

The Company does not have significant equity investments that are publicly traded. The Company does not have significant non-listed equity securities that are susceptible to market price risk arising from uncertainties about future values of the investment securities. The Company manages its investment in unquoted securities by monitoring the cash flow measures.
